articles.title: Why has Brittany Mahomes stopped posing warmly with Patrick Mahomes’ younger brother Jackson Mahomes
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes used to be a frequent visitor on her brother-in-law Jackson Mahomes’ Instagram account.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes used to be a frequent visitor on her brother-in-law Jackson Mahomes’ Instagram account.However, since the 2026 NFL season began, Patrick Mahomes’ brother hasn’t posted any photos with the mother of three. Even his most recent IG post features one of Brittany’s children rather than Brittany herself.While Brittany appeared in nearly every other photo from June 2019 until September 2025, she has rarely been featured since. Currently, only a few pictures on his Instagram include her, and in those, she appears alongside the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback, his mother Randi Mahomes, and his half-sister Mia Randall.Brittany Mahomes and Jackson Mahomes’ changing relationshipBrittany Mahomes went from wearing the brightest smile while posing with Jackson Mahomes to sporting a subtle, “not-interested-in-posing-with-you” look over the course of six years.On the other hand, Jackson’s smile never changed in the slightest; he looks just as radiant as he did in their very first photo together. However, Brittany’s shifting attitude toward her brother-in-law is now impossible to miss.He was there helping her choose her wedding dress, celebrating her birthdays, and helping take care of her kids. But now? Suddenly, everything has changed.Fans were so used to seeing them together that when Jackson appeared to hard-launch his relationship with Shyanne Blankenship on Instagram, one user commented, “Ain’t that Brittany Mahomes?”Another wrote, “Looks like big bro’s wife,” while a third added, “Resemble Brittany.” A fourth user simply asked, “Why does that look like Brittany?” That is just how frequently the two used to post together.Maybe his Kansas City influencer girlfriend dislikes him posing with his brother’s wife on Instagram, though that is pure speculation. Ultimately, anything could explain the drop in posts.Alternatively, maybe Brittany disapproves of Jackson dating Shyanne Blankenship, leading her to stop posing with him with her signature bright smile.Jackson’s 2021 birthday post for Brittany read, “HBD to my bestie/sidekick and future sister. Loved celebrating you.” If Brittany was once that close to him, maybe she dislikes his current girlfriend - or maybe she is simply too busy managing three children and several multimillion-dollar business ventures.Or did that viral 2024 Super Bowl party video have something to do with a potential fallout? Jackson appeared to be denied entry into a VIP section during a Future concert in Las Vegas, right where his sister-in-law was standing.When the security guard blocked Jackson, he looked in Brittany’s direction, seemingly hoping she would intervene. Instead, she shrugged and kept dancing.Or did Kayla Nicole have something to do with the fallout between the two?Brittany Mahomes’ constant presence on Jackson Mahomes’ InstagramEvery year, the wife of the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has appeared alongside members of the Mahomes family at football games and several of their celebrations.Jackson has shared updates and personal moments from those celebrations with his Instagram followers, maintaining a strong social media presence over the past six years.He has also posed with Kayla Nicole, Travis Kelce’s ex-girlfriend and Brittany’s former close friend. Their previous public appearances have included family celebrations and football-related events.In May 2025, Jackson reposted Brittany’s Instagram story, in which the NFL WAG posed in a risque, one-shouldered dress and sat alongside her friend Miranda and Jackson. She captioned it, “Happy Birthdayyyy!!!!! [Jackson Mahomes].”Jackson Mahomes’ Instagram posts spark rift speculationBeing part of a high-profile NFL family means even slight changes in social media activity attract widespread public scrutiny.Patrick Mahomes’ career with the Kansas City Chiefs has kept the Mahomes family in the spotlight for nearly a decade. On the other hand, Brittany Mahomes has created her own public profile through business ventures, fitness, and lifestyle content on her social media account.Consequently, a smaller number of joint photos cannot reliably measure family closeness or indicate a rift. articles.body: Aaron Rodgers may have finally started putting his family drama behind him, but it looks like there are still a few awkward chapters left in the Rodgers family story. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback's long-awaited reunion with his family was supposed to mark a fresh start. However, a new report is raising questions about just how close everyone really is, especially when it comes to his younger brother, Jordan Rodgers, and his mystery wife, Brittani.Aaron Rodgers’ family reunion not so picture-perfect? Brother Jordan reportedly knows little about mystery wifeAccording to a new report, an insider claims that Jordan and his wife, JoJo Fletcher, don't seem to know much about Brittani. The source also hinted that the relationship between the brothers might not be completely back on track, despite their recent efforts to reconnect.And honestly, that detail makes this family reunion story even more interesting. Aaron has credited Brittani with helping him open the door to reconciliation, yet his brother's reported lack of familiarity with her suggests that the family's journey toward healing could be more complicated than it looks.Aaron's relationship with his family has been a topic of conversation for years. The quarterback's estrangement from his parents and siblings became public knowledge during Jordan's appearance on The Bachelorette in 2016, when Jordan spoke about their distant relationship.For a long time, there were few signs of a meaningful reconciliation. That began to change this year, when Aaron shared glimpses of spending time with his parents and older brother, Luke.The quarterback later opened up about reconnecting with Jordan, too. During an appearance on Cam Heyward's Not Just Football podcast in September, Aaron confirmed that the brothers had met and described their conversation as a tough one.Brittani is perhaps the most intriguing person in this story because Aaron has kept his marriage largely out of the public eye. Aaron confirmed that he was married in June 2025, but has deliberately kept details about his wife private. Unlike many celebrity couples, the two have largely avoided sharing their relationship with the world.Aaron has credited Brittani with helping him become more open to repairing his family relationships. Her encouragement reportedly played a role in his decision to reconnect with his parents and siblings after years of estrangement.That's what makes the insider's claim about Jordan and JoJo particularly interesting. If the report is accurate, Aaron's wife has been an important figure in his reconciliation journey, while his younger brother's household apparently remains unfamiliar with her.Earlier reporting also indicated that Jordan and JoJo did not attend Aaron's wedding. However, neither that absence nor the latest insider comments independently prove that Brittani is the reason behind any lingering tension.Jordan Rodgers has shown public support for his brotherDespite their complicated history, Jordan hasn't appeared entirely disconnected from Aaron.Jordan publicly defended his brother's football performance during an appearance on ESPN's First Take in September, praising Aaron's play and discussing the expectations surrounding the Steelers.Jordan also liked a family post shared by their older brother Luke after a Steelers gathering, even though he wasn't pictured with the group. Those gestures don't reveal what is happening behind closed doors, but they do offer a more nuanced picture than a simple story of two brothers falling out all over again.Jordan and JoJo also have their own lives and commitments, making it difficult to draw conclusions from their absence at a family gathering. articles.title: 49ers’ perfect DeForest Buckner trade offer to Colts before NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers should offer the Indianapolis Colts a 2027 third-round pick for DeForest Buckner before the November 10 NFL trade deadline. That is a...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers should offer the Indianapolis Colts a 2027 third-round pick for DeForest Buckner before the November 10 NFL trade deadline. That is a meaningful price for a 32-year-old defensive tackle, but his production and fit make a reunion worth pursuing.

This would not be about correcting an unpopular decision from six years ago. It would be about acquiring an interior difference-maker for a championship push while giving Indianapolis a valuable asset for its next roster overhaul.

Why Buckner would elevate San Francisco's defensive front

Buckner has recorded 26 tackles, four sacks and three passes defended through six games in 2026. He also has eight quarterback hits and four tackles for loss. Those numbers show a veteran still influencing possessions rather than surviving on reputation.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

That interior disruption is what San Francisco should prioritize. Edge pressure becomes more dangerous when quarterbacks cannot comfortably step forward, and Buckner can challenge guards while creating less predictable escape routes.

His arrival would also broaden the defensive coordinator's options. The 49ers could pursue pressure with four rushers more confidently, preserving additional defenders in coverage instead of depending on extra blitzers to manufacture disruption.

There is a run-defense benefit, too. Buckner's ability to penetrate can force runners to alter their paths before reaching the second level. That creates opportunities for teammates, provided the entire front maintains its gap responsibilities.

Familiarity adds appeal without eliminating the adjustment period. Buckner spent his first four NFL seasons with San Francisco, and Kyle Juszczyk has publicly encouraged him to return. Existing relationships could help his integration, although the current scheme and personnel still require study.

The contract creates urgency and risk. Buckner is in the final year of his deal, so San Francisco would be acquiring immediate help without guaranteed control beyond this season. An extension could be discussed separately, but the trade should make sense even without one.

Why Indianapolis should consider moving its defensive leader

The Colts are 2-4, making their deadline decision more complicated than simply declaring themselves contenders or sellers. Trading Buckner would weaken the defense immediately and remove an established locker-room presence.

Still, Indianapolis must weigh that loss against the possibility of watching him leave in free agency. A guaranteed third-round selection would provide a concrete return now rather than relying on an uncertain future compensatory-pick outcome.

That selection could help address several needs. The Colts could draft a replacement defender, strengthen another position or use it as part of a larger transaction. Younger contributors on rookie contracts would give the organization greater flexibility around its next core.

Financial considerations matter, but neither team should confuse Buckner's full 2026 cap charge with the amount transferred in a deadline trade. Previously paid bonus accounting and remaining compensation require separate analysis before any agreement.

The perfect offer balances impact against rental risk

The proposed package should remain straightforward:

San Francisco's 2027 third-round draft pick.

For Indianapolis, a third-rounder acknowledges that Buckner remains a premium contributor rather than a veteran being discarded. For San Francisco, it preserves first- and second-round selections while addressing an immediate need with a proven player.

The 49ers should resist adding another substantial asset unless competing bids justify it. Buckner's age and expiring contract impose a sensible ceiling, even with his strong performance.

This is the kind of calculated aggression contenders should embrace: pay for present impact, respect the long-term cost and avoid letting familiarity replace disciplined evaluation.

articles.title: Jason Kelce praises Chiefs fan for making a Caitlin Clark-style basketball shot
articles.summary: Jason Kelce praised a Kansas City Chiefs fan after a successful long-range basketball shot at a pregame tailgate on Oct. 18, 2026. The New Heights podcast co...
articles.body:
Jason Kelce had a memorable moment with Kansas City Chiefs fans ahead of the team's Oct. 18, 2026, game against the Los Angeles Chargers. During a pregame tailgate outside Arrowhead Stadium, the retired NFL center watched a fan sink an unusually long basketball shot and immediately connected the moment to WNBA star Caitlin Clark.

Kelce, who co-hosts the popular New Heights podcast with his brother, Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, was interacting with fans during the event when the impressive attempt found its mark. The podcast's official social media account celebrated the moment by referencing Clark's renowned long-range shooting.

The playful comparison brought together two major sports audiences: NFL fans who gathered to support Kansas City and basketball followers familiar with Clark's ability to make shots from well beyond the three-point line. It also highlighted the growing connection between Clark and the Kelce family.

Jason Kelce's pregame event delivered an unexpected highlight

Kelce's interaction with Chiefs supporters took place during a New Heights tailgate ahead of Kansas City's matchup with the Chargers. The event gave fans an opportunity to meet the retired Philadelphia Eagles center and participate in activities before kickoff.

One basketball challenge produced the afternoon's standout moment. As a fan prepared to attempt a distant shot, Kelce provided running commentary, building anticipation as the ball traveled toward the basket.

The attempt went in, prompting an enthusiastic reaction from Kelce. Rather than treating the successful shot as an ordinary tailgate highlight, he helped turn it into a memorable moment by linking the fan's range to one of basketball's most recognizable shooters.

The fan's long-range shot earned a Caitlin Clark comparison

Kelce's commentary included the line, "Here it comes, all the way from New York City," as the fan launched the ball. The exaggerated description captured the distance involved and added to the excitement surrounding the attempt.

After the shot went through the basket, the New Heights account shared the clip with the caption, "From Caitlin Clark range." The post tagged Clark, making the Indiana Fever star part of the moment even though she was not the person taking the shot.

The comparison was a natural fit for Clark's reputation as an ambitious long-range shooter. Her ability to launch deep 3-pointers has become a defining feature of her game, making her name an easy reference for fans who have seen her connect from far away.

Caitlin Clark's shooting range has become part of her identity

Clark rose to national prominence at the University of Iowa, where her scoring ability and deep shooting helped attract unprecedented attention to women's college basketball. Her performances made long-range attempts a signature part of her on-court identity.

She carried that reputation into the WNBA with the Indiana Fever. Clark's willingness to shoot from well beyond the conventional 3-point range forces defenders to account for her farther from the basket, creating opportunities for teammates as well as herself.

The tailgate comparison was a lighthearted reference, not a claim that the fan's shot was equivalent to Clark's performance in a competitive game. Still, it illustrated how recognizable her shooting style has become beyond women's basketball.

Clark's connection to the Chiefs made the reference even better

Clark is not simply a basketball star being mentioned by an NFL personality. She has openly supported the Kansas City Chiefs for years, giving her a genuine connection to the team whose fans attended Kelce's event.

The Iowa native has discussed her Chiefs fandom publicly, and her friendship with the Kelce family has helped bring her into the team's wider circle. Her appearances alongside Taylor Swift at Chiefs games have also attracted attention.

That overlap made the reference especially fitting for a Kansas City tailgate. A basketball shot became an opportunity to recognize a player whose interests extend beyond her own sport and whose connection with the Chiefs is well established.

Jason and Travis Kelce have built a relationship with Clark

Clark previously appeared on New Heights , where she discussed basketball, her life outside the game and her enthusiasm for the Chiefs. The conversation gave listeners a chance to see her interact with the brothers beyond the usual boundaries of sports coverage.

The Kelces have also shown interest in Clark's career away from the podcast studio. Their public exchanges reflect a friendly relationship that brings together professional football, women's basketball, and the broader sports-entertainment world.

That familiarity helps explain why Clark's name came naturally into the tailgate moment. The reference was more than a random celebrity comparison; it connected a successful fan shot to a basketball player the Kelce brothers already know.

The moment highlighted the crossover between football and basketball

Professional sports audiences often overlap, particularly when athletes and personalities share interests across leagues. Clark's Chiefs fandom is one example of how a prominent basketball player can also become part of the conversation surrounding an NFL team.

Kelce's tailgate appearance provided a relaxed setting for that crossover. Fans were not watching a formal competition between professional athletes; they were participating in a pregame gathering where a spontaneous moment could become a highlight.

The clip also demonstrated how a short social media post can connect different sports communities. A fan's long shot, Kelce's enthusiastic commentary and a reference to Clark combined to make a simple activity more memorable.

The New Heights tailgate added to the Chiefs' game-day atmosphere

The New Heights event was part of the buildup to Kansas City's Oct. 18 home game against the Chargers. Kelce's presence gave attendees a chance to engage with a familiar football personality before the teams took the field.

The tailgate included fan-focused activities and a meet-and-greet opportunity with Jason Kelce. Such gatherings allow supporters to connect with sports figures in a setting that feels more personal than a stadium seat or television broadcast.

For Kelce, the basketball challenge offered an unscripted highlight amid the day's scheduled activities. The fan made the shot, Kelce supplied the excitement, and the podcast account gave the moment a memorable connection to Clark.

Clark's growing influence reaches beyond the basketball court

Clark's impact is evident not only in the attention paid to her games but also in how her name is recognized across sports. Her deep shooting has become a shorthand reference that audiences can understand even outside a basketball arena.

Her presence in the Chiefs conversation reflects the same wider appeal. As a prominent Fever player and an established Kansas City supporter, Clark can connect with fans who follow football as closely as they follow basketball.

Fun fact: Caitlin Clark's Chiefs fandom inspired the red "Sea of Red" colorway of her signature Nike Caitlin 1 basketball shoe, which Travis Kelce received as a gift from the WNBA star.

The Steelers described the decision as a precaution after the Bastille area experienced recent disruptions. Additional demonstrations could also take place in Paris and other areas of France over the weekend.

The NFL's broader activities in the city have continued without interruption. Nicki Ewell, the league's vice president for global events, told the AP that Pittsburgh made the call to cancel Steelers House. The NFL helped distribute the announcement after previously working with the team to promote the gathering.

Ewell said other NFL fan events have not been affected.

An Irish pub called O'Sullivans in the Bastille area had also advertised a watch party for Sunday's Steelers-Saints matchup.

Roger Goodell addresses security ahead of Steelers' Paris clash

The Steelers reiterated that the league continues to coordinate with local officials as preparations for the game continue.

"The NFL, as they do for every game, including international games, is working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters," the Steelers said in a statement to the AP. "As stated by the NFL, there have been no disruptions or impacts at League sites."

NFL commissioner Roger Goodell addressed the unrest Wednesday and expressed confidence that the league has taken the necessary precautions for its Paris game.

Goodell said he spoke with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, while officials have remained in communication with authorities in Paris and throughout France.

"We've made all the preparations," Goodell said. "Protests are not unusual in France, as you know, and that's something that we will be aware of and make sure that the appropriate arrangements are made."

The cancellation therefore remains limited to Pittsburgh's designated Bastille bar event rather than Sunday's game.

The Steelers enter Week 7 at 4-2, while the Saints sit at 2-4. Pittsburgh and New Orleans will meet Sunday at Stade de France, with kickoff scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network.

articles.title: Ravens' Marlon Humphrey Calls Out Lamar Jackson 'Slander,' Says QB Gets 'Unfair Treatment'
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey defended teammate and quarterback Lamar Jackson on Thursday in a chat with reporters.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey defended teammate and quarterback Lamar Jackson on Thursday in a chat with reporters.

"It seems like Lamar's the only quarterback kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on," Humphrey said, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley . "I feel like you just don't see these same articles. I'm in the hot tub and it's this, that and the third. Unfair treatment."

Per Hensley, Humphrey was asked if he was referencing injury "slander." Hensley said Humphrey didn't specify, but the four-time Pro Bowler added the following remarks:

"I just feel like sometimes it seems like it gets away from ... I don't know if it's because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him. But I do know this, if Lamar Jackson can play, if he's healthy enough to play, he will play, and that's kind of all I can say for that."

One can perhaps safely guess Humphrey was referring to critics of Jackson who bemoan his absences from the lineup, including this year.

Jackson suffered a left ankle sprain on October 4 in the first half of his team's 23-17 win over the Tennessee Titans. He missed the remainder of that contest and the Ravens' next two games against the Atlanta Falcons (31-23 win) and Cleveland Browns (13-10 loss).

Jackson turned in limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday this week in advance of the team's home game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jackson has dealt with numerous injuries over the years and missed time, although he's still been in the lineup far more often than not since becoming the Ravens' QB1 in the middle of the 2018 season.

From 2019-2025, Jackson started 100 of a possible 117 games. He missed five games apiece in 2021 and 2022 but played every game in 2023 and 2024 minus the 2023 regular season opener, which occurred after Baltimore had already secured the AFC's No. 1 seed.

Jackson missed four games last year (three due to a hamstring injury, one due to a back contusion) and ultimately was slowed down by ailments overall .

Unfortunately, Jackson has now dealt with a new injury, but it appears he's at least trending in the right direction for a massive AFC North battle with the Bengals.

articles.title: New Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors as Colts RB Talks Potential Deal Before NFL Deadline
articles.summary: With the Indianapolis Colts off to a 2-4 start to the season, a handful of teams reportedly are eyeing star running back Jonathan Taylor.
articles.body:
With the Indianapolis Colts off to a 2-4 start to the season, a handful of teams reportedly are eyeing star running back Jonathan Taylor.

Per ESPN's Stephen Holder , several teams "would be open to a potential trade" for Taylor, but it is to be determined whether the Colts will look to be sellers at the deadline.

As his name begins to swirl in trade rumors, Taylor said his focus is on Indianapolis' upcoming matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.

NFL Insiders Name 'Sleeper' Trade Targets

"I haven't given any thought," he said when asked about his future. "That'd be crazy right now, especially because we've got a great Minnesota Vikings team that we have to go against. I think it would be a discredit and a disservice to my teammates and this whole organization to think about what could, what should, what may be."

The report follows the Colts' firing of general manager Chris Ballard earlier this week. Ballard drafted Taylor out of Wisconsin in 2020 and signed him to two contracts, including a two-year, $44 million extension in August.

Taylor has played up to the extension so far, recording the second-most carries (122) for the sixth-most rushing yards (492) and the second-most touchdowns (7).

But with the Colts struggling so far this season, and potential changes coming after Ballard's firing, it could be in the team's best interest to trade their star player and start building for the future.

The trade deadline is on Nov. 10, which doesn't give Indianapolis a lot of time to turn into a playoff contender. The Colts will face the undefeated Vikings this week before taking on the 4-2 Jacksonville Jaguars next week.

Along with Taylor, Holder noted that DeForest Buckner is another name that could be on the move before the deadline. The star defensive tackle has already picked up four sacks this season.

Buckner, who has been with the team since 2020, was clearly frustrated after the Colts' loss to the Tennessee Titans on Sunday.

"I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters after the loss.

Perhaps moving on from Ballard will spark some new life in the Colts as they look to turn things around, but if things keep trending in the wrong direction, it could be the end of Taylor and more players' tenures in Indianapolis.

articles.title: Marshall Faulk Reveals Parkinson's Diagnosis, NFL Legend and Southern HC Says He's 'In a Good Place'
articles.summary: Pro Football Hall of Fame running back and Southern University football head coach Marshall Faulk revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.
articles.body:
Pro Football Hall of Fame running back and Southern University football head coach Marshall Faulk revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

Faulk revealed the news on Dr. Sandeep Thakka's "Caring Neurologist" podcast.

The former Indianapolis Colts and St. Louis Rams superstar said he has been dealing with symptoms of the disease for a year-and-a-half. He first noticed an issue while he was playing golf.

"The rigidity in my hand, just sometimes after I play a lot or I practice a lot," Faulk said, per Toyloy Brown III of The Advocate . "I just thought it was, you know, normal nerves when putting and stuff like that."

During a biannual physical, Faulk's doctor advised him to get the situation checked out. A diagnosis followed, but thankfully, Faulk said he received his diagnosis in the early stages of the disease and considers himself "one of the lucky ones" for doing so.

Numerous ex-NFL players have revealed neurodegenerative disease diagnoses in recent years.

Of note, quarterback Brett Favre (in 2024) and running back Ahman Green (in 2026) told the public they were diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

Running back Chris Johnson revealed last June that he has been diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (Lou Gehrig's disease).

The 53-year-old Faulk was one of his generation's greatest players. He was a versatile running back equally adept at rushing and receiving. Over his 12-year career (1994-2005), Faulk amassed 12,279 rushing yards and 6,875 receiving yards for 19,154 yards from scrimmage, ranking fifth all time in that category.

During the Rams' 1999 Super Bowl season, Faulk broke the 1,000-yard barrier in rushing (1,381 yards) and receiving (1,048 yards). He is one of three running backs to ever do so in a single season (Roger Craig, 1985; Christian McCaffrey, 2019).

Faulk was a first-ballot Hall of Famer, inducted as part of the class of 2011. He is also a member of the College Football Hall of Fame after his time at San Diego State (5,562 all-purpose yards, 62 career touchdowns, 1992 Heisman Trophy runner-up).

Faulk served as Colorado's running backs coach last year before becoming Southern's head coach this season. The 3-4 Jaguars have already eclipsed last year's two-win total.

articles.title: The Lions’ heavy offense will stretch the Packers’ thin defensive line
articles.summary: Can Green Bay win another game with just four interior defensive linemen? Detroit will be a big test
articles.body:
You've heard this phrase a lot in the NFL over the last decade: Nickel is the new base. In some ways that's true, but it's really more like "nickel is the new base, when the opposing offense wants it to be."

Most NFL teams still match their defensive personnel to what opposing offenses throw out there, and the Green Bay Packers are no different. In general, defenses want to play as many cornerbacks and nickelbacks as the opposing offense has receivers.

So when offenses are in 11 personnel (three receivers, one back and one tight end) sets, defenses tend to play Nickel — which allows for a slot defender to "match" a slot receiver on the field. So far in 2026, the Packers have played 291 of their 292 snaps when they've faced 11 personnel offenses in Nickel (or Dime) sets — 99.7 percent.

When opposing offenses play heavier looks, be it multiple backs, multiple tight ends or even sets with extra offensive linemen or defensive linemen, NFL teams still match that with "base" personnel (a 3-4 in the Packers' case) an extra body in the box.

This year, Green Bay defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon's defense has played 75.9 percent of their snaps against these personnel packages (12/13/21/22) with a base 3-4 defense. No third receiver? That means no slot defender on the field. That's the basic math being done league-wide.

So is nickel the new base? Really only when the offense is playing 11 personnel. This, obviously, varies a lot team-by-team.

For example, last week the Packers faced the Dallas Cowboys, who have played 73 percent of their snaps in 11 personnel in 2026, the third-highest rate in the NFL . Against Green Bay, for whatever reason, they averaged 1.0 running backs per play and 1.1 tight ends per play — essentially living in 11 personnel full-time, even more so than their season-long averages.

From my perspective, I feel like the Packers caught a break. Green Bay, which almost always carries five interior defensive linemen on a 48-man gameday roster, was only able to carry four big bodies for the game because of Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford going on the injured reserve. Rookie Chris McClellan had to take over the starting 3-4 nose tackle spot in "base" looks for the first time, in place of Ford, and the only defensive lineman on the sideline when the starters were out there for limited 3-4 defense looks was Anthony Campbell, who had played all of nine career NFL snaps coming into the game. On top of that, Green Bay's Will linebacker position is a rotation between Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper right now, as starter Edgerrin Cooper is now on the injured reserve.

Campbell ended up playing 32 defensive snaps for the Packers in Week 6, even with the Cowboys playing mostly 11 personnel looks that mostly kept Green Bay to playing two defensive tackles at a time for most of the game. With how the Packers' lack of depth at the position played out on the defensive line, Dallas should have tried to wear out Green Bay's lack of numbers with multiple tight end looks (with slot defender Javon Bullard sidelined because of personnel matching) and tried to win that game in the second half against an exhausted front. Instead, Bullard played six of every seven snaps against the Cowboys.

The Packers dodged a bullet, but that doesn't mean that they're out of the woods. This week, they'll play a Detroit Lions team that likes to play a much heavier form of offense than Dallas. The Lions only play 11 personnel 58 percent of the time, a below-average rate in the NFL. They like to use multiple tight ends, or even linemen (both offensive or defensive) instead of that extra slot receiver.

They don't use multiple backs (average 1.0 backs played per play), but they play a second tight end (or extra lineman) close to every other play (1.5 tight ends per play).

It will be interesting to see if the Packers call up one of their two practice squad interior defensive linemen, David Blay Jr. or Mazi Smith, to add some depth to the game-day roster this week, but if Green Bay doesn't, they'll have to make it through with four linemen for a second straight game. This time, though, they won't be playing against a team that just wants to play with a full-time slot receiver, they'll be going against an offense that wants to play heavy offensive looks about every other play, the same looks that have forced an extra defensive lineman on the field for more than three-quarters of the Packers' defensive snaps in those situations throughout the season.

articles.summary: The Bears returned home for the first time since Mike Ditka's death. Take a look at how the team paid tribute to the legend.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears returned home for the first time since NFL Hall of Famer Mike Ditka died at the age of 86 on Oct. 9 . A representative of Ditka's told USA TODAY that he died of natural causes .

Best known as the coach of the Super Bowl champion 1985 Bears, Ditka was a force to be reckoned with between the white lines too.

He helped revolutionize the tight end position, etching his name into NFL history as both a player and coach.

The Bears paid tribute to Ditka ahead of a "Thursday Night Football" matchup against the New England Patriots on Oct. 22.

Of course, Ditka's iconic mustache was a key part of the tribute. The Bears gave away mustaches as part of a stadium-wide giveaway at Soldier Field.

In addition to a helmet decal, Ditka's No. 89 was painted on the field at the stadium.

The Bears announced that there would be other fan activations, on-field recognition and moments honoring the legendary coach in addition to the tribute.

articles.title: Marshall Faulk discloses Parkinson's disease diagnosis
articles.summary: Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has disclosed that he has Parkinson's disease.
articles.body:
Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has disclosed that he has Parkinson's disease.

Via Jack Baer of Yahoo Sports, Faulk revealed the diagnosis in an appearance on the Caring Neurologist podcast.

"I get a physical twice a year," Faulk said. "I'm a little anal about my health. I literally asked my doctor because I noticed it as I was playing golf. I noticed the rigidity in my hand after I play a lot or practice a lot, I thought it was just normal nerves when putting and stuff like that. But it started to be times where I wasn't playing — I mean, where I was playing, but I wasn't in a match, and it would still do that.

"I was like, 'Wow, is that something? Is that normal?' And the doctor was like, ' You need to go get checked . You need to go have X, Y and Z done.'"

Faulk, a former NFL MVP, two-time NFL Offensive Player of the Year, three-time first-team All-Pro, and seven-time Pro Bowler, has been receiving treatment and taking medication.

"Since I've started on the medication, I don't really have a lot of issues," Faulk said. "I might sleep a little more. . . . Other than that, the rigidity in my hands, I still have that. Can't say that it's gotten worse. The little tremors that I get, they are what they are. I just pay attention to my gait, how I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is.

"I don't look at it as something that's terminal. It's like, 'Hey, you get to live with this.' There's far worse things out there."

There's a known link between Parkinson's disease and football. It's one of the specific conditions that make a player who retired prior to the final settlement of the concussion class action automatically eligible for payment.

articles.title: Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield drops confident declaration on clawing back into NFC South race
articles.summary: Baker Mayfield has motivation to get the Tampa Bay Buccaneers back on track following a poor start to the 2026 NFL season. Mayfield has been playing in the l...
articles.body:
Baker Mayfield has motivation to get the Tampa Bay Buccaneers back on track following a poor start to the 2026 NFL season.

Mayfield has been playing in the league since 2018, going through his fourth season with the Buccaneers. He stands out as one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL, often helping Tampa Bay be in the mix for playoff contention.

However, the start to the 2026 season has been brutal for the squad. They have lost five of their first six games, being one of the worst performing teams in the league early on. It didn't help matters that Mayfield dislocated his thumb in Week 3, sidelining him for the next three games.

Mayfield has made significant progress with his health, conversing with media on Thursday. He is taking his timeline patiently, looking forward to getting Tampa Bay back with winning momentum for the remainder of the 2026 season.

"We've got to take it one game at a time, and you know our opponent this week is the one leading division, and so we got to take care of business this week, and that's all that matters," Mayfield said, per reporter Rick Stroud. "It's going to be early on to be a one game at a time mentality, but listen, our guys are ready for it, and we'll see what happens."

What lies ahead for Baker Mayfield, Buccaneers

Baker Mayfield knows the stakes that are in play with the Buccaneers needing to return to the playoffs. However, their poor start won't cut it if they wish to bounce back in convincing fashion.

Tampa Bay has a 1-5 record this season, being at the bottom of the NFC South Division standings. They are behind the New Orleans Saints and the Atlanta Falcons at the moment. In terms of the conference standings, they are last place. They are under the Washington Commanders and the Los Angeles Rams.

The Buccaneers will continue preparations for their upcoming matchup, being on the road. They take on the Carolina Panthers in Week 7 as kickoff commences on Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Mark Sanchez’s change-of-plea hearing rescheduled to 2027, case reassigned to new judge
articles.summary: The long and winding legal road for Mark Sanchez, following an incident in Indianapolis that ended with him in the hospital, is going to continue for a bit l...
articles.body:
The long and winding legal road for Mark Sanchez, following an incident in Indianapolis that ended with him in the hospital, is going to continue for a bit longer.

After several court-date delays , Sanchez pleaded guilty last month , though it was unknown which charges he was pleading guilty to; among those he faced were battery causing serious injury, unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, and public intoxication. A change-of-plea hearing in the criminal case was scheduled for Nov. 9 in Marion Superior Court.

However, this one too has been rescheduled.

According to Austin Hanson at Fox 59 , Sanchez's change-of-plea hearing has been moved. While changes in Indiana's public court reporting system on Wednesday initially suggested that the hearing had been canceled, further additions on Thursday confirmed the hearing had been rescheduled to Jan. 25, 2027.

Also noted in the Thursday update was that the judge assigned to the case, Helen W. Marchal, recused herself , though no reason was given for the recusal. The January hearing will take place before Judge Angela Dow Davis.

Sanchez, who was in Indianapolis to call a Colts game on Oct. 5 last year, was involved in a violent altercation outside his hotel with 69-year-old truck driver Perry Tole. The former NFL quarterback, who is believed to have been intoxicated , allegedly confronted the man inside the cab of his delivery truck. Tole, who claimed he believed his life was in danger, pepper-sprayed and stabbed Sanchez in self-defense. Both men were hospitalized after the incident. Fox Sports suspended Sanchez and later fired him .

Sanchez and former employer Fox also faced a civil suit stemming from the incident. According to court records, he and Tole reached an agreement in principle that will end the civil suit against the former NFL quarterback. Tole's attorneys are expected to file a motion to dismiss the civil case by Jan. 8.

articles.title: NFL Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk reveals Parkinson's diagnosis
articles.summary: The former Rams star discussed the diagnosis in a podcast episode.
articles.body:
Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk announced Thursday that he is battling Parkinson's disease.

Faulk, who won a Super Bowl and an MVP award as part of the "Greatest Show on Turf" Rams teams, made the announcement on "The Caring Neurologist" podcast with Dr. Sandeep Thakkar.

The 53-year-old isn't alone in fighting the disease, as Hall of Fame QB Brett Favre disclosed a Parkinson's diagnosis in 2024 and fellow running back Ahman Green also revealed a diagnosis earlier this year.

Here's what Faulk had to say about his condition.

Marshall Faulk reveals Parkinson's diagnosis

Faulk, who is the head football coach at FCS Southern University, revealed Thursday that he is battling Parkinson's disease, adding that he is still living a normal life in part because it was detected so early.

"Since I've started on the medication, I don't really have a lot of issues," Faulk said, explaining that he just has "little tremors" at the moment.

"I just pay attention to my gait, while I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance," Faulk said. "It's still where it is."

Faulk explained that he started to notice symptoms in his hand and was told by his doctor to get a closer evaluation when he brought it up during a physical.

"The rigidity in my hand, just sometimes after I play a lot or I practice a lot," Faulk said. "I just thought it was, you know, normal nerves when putting and stuff like that."

Faulk released a lengthier statement after appearing on the podcast:

Fortunately, Faulk said the early detection will give him a better quality of life going forward. Here's what you need to know about the disease.

Parkinson's disease is a progressive nervous system disorder that is not curable. While individuals with Parkinson's will have to live with it for the rest of their lives and face worsening symptoms as time progresses, the average lifespan of a person with the disease is not significantly reduced.

The most recognizable Parkinson's symptom is tremors in the arms and hands, according to the Mayo Clinic . Patients can also develop stiffness in the muscles that impacts their abilty to walk normally and raises the risk of falls.

Researchers from Boston University revealed in 2025 that they had found a connection between playing football and a higher risk of Parkinson's disease. Faulk joins Brett Favre, Ahman Green and Bernie Kosar as notable former players with the condition.

They have since turned it around and won three consecutive games, positioning themselves as legitimate AFC East contenders.

The Bears, meanwhile, have started three different quarterbacks through six weeks after a hamstring injury sidelined Caleb Williams for three games. Williams returned for last week's win over the Falcons , and he clearly made an impact on the offense.
